sources.entry: Speedtest Tracker - Monitor the performance and uptime of your internet connection. (Source Code) MIT Docker/K8S
Speedtest Tracker | Track your internet speed over time

summary.one_liner: Speedtest Tracker is a self-hosted application that schedules internet speed tests and records performance and uptime over time.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a self-hosted app that runs scheduled speed tests against your internet connection. It captures download and upload speeds, ping, and packet loss. Results are stored as historical data so you can view trends and spot patterns in connection problems. It can send notifications when performance drops below a configured threshold. The UI is available in multiple languages through community translations on Crowdin. The README points to separate guides for Docker installation, NAS platforms (Synology and Unraid), configuration, notification channels, and FAQs, which are not included in the README itself.
use_cases: get alerts when speed falls below threshold
run scheduled speed tests on a server or NAS
how_to_run: Deploy the Docker image (built by LinuxServer.io), following the installation guide linked from the README
notable: Scheduled automated speed tests with historical trend data
Captures download, upload, ping and packet loss
Documented deployment on Synology and Unraid NAS platforms
caveats: README is brief and defers installation, configuration and FAQ details to separate guides not included here
Deployment is documented mainly around Docker containers
